name: NJ-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Norcross holds an overwhelming cash advantage, about $2.38 million to roughly $2,000 for Galdo
The district leans Democratic by about ten points
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings exist, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The D+10 district, Norcross's roughly hundred-to-one financial edge, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to a safe Democratic hold, and nothing in the record suggests Galdo has the resources to compete.
model.watch: A wave of outside spending against Norcross or credible polling showing a single-digit race would justify moving this toward the competitive range.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Jersey's first district leans about ten points Democratic, and Representative Donald Norcross returns as a well-funded incumbent. He reports more than $2.3 million on hand, while Republican Damon Galdo has raised under $16,000 and had roughly $2,000 in cash in mid-year filings. No outside groups are opposing the incumbent, and no public polls or expert ratings track the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and campaign finance.

Prediction markets price Norcross's re-election around 96 percent, reflecting his financial edge and the district's lean. A favorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the margin, but with no visible challenger operation or outside opposition, the expected outcome is a comfortable double-digit Democratic win. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the size of the margin less certain than its direction.
